name: azure_managed_redis
description:
Manages an Azure Managed Redis (Redis Enterprise) instance, provisioned within an environment and resource group.

Azure models this as two ARM resources and the platform creates both: a `Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise` cluster (SKU, TLS, high availability, public network access) and a single `Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/databases` child named `default` (clustering policy, eviction policy, modules, persistence, geo-replication, access-key auth). The attributes below are flattened across both. The database child is created only after the cluster finishes provisioning, so `database_id` and the access-key operations are unavailable for a period after the resource first reports Complete — set `wait_for_database` if you need to depend on them.

attributes.name: workspace_id
attributes.description: ID of the workspace that owns this Redis instance.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Redis instance name. 1-60 characters, alphanumeric and hyphens, first and last character alphanumeric, no consecutive hyphens, and globally unique across Azure. Immutable after creation.

attributes.name: environment_id
attributes.description: ID of the environment in which the Redis instance is provisioned.

attributes.name: resource_group_id
attributes.description: ID of the resource group in which the Redis instance is provisioned.

attributes.name: scope_ids
attributes.description: Scope IDs linking this Redis instance to a cloud provider account, inherited from the resource group.

attributes.name: sku_name
attributes.description:
Azure Managed Redis SKU. Cache size is fixed by the SKU name across all four supported families (Balanced, MemoryOptimized, ComputeOptimized, FlashOptimized). Immutable after creation.

The legacy `Enterprise_*` and `EnterpriseFlash_*` families are deliberately not offered: those are Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise SKUs, which Azure has retired — a create returns "Creation of new Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise resources is no longer supported". They are therefore unusable here, including for adopting an existing legacy instance.

attributes.name: minimum_tls_version
attributes.description: Minimum TLS version the cluster accepts. `Tls1_2` is the only accepted value — TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are obsolete on Azure Managed Redis and the API rejects them. The attribute exists so the value is explicit in configuration and state, and so a future version can be added without a breaking change.

attributes.name: high_availability
attributes.description: Replicate the data set within the cluster. Enabled by default, which is also what `persistence` and `geo_replication` require — setting this to `false` makes either of them fail. Disabling it lowers the availability SLA and increases the risk of data loss.

attributes.name: public_network_access_enabled
attributes.description: Expose the cluster's public endpoint. Defaults to disabled per platform policy, in which case the cluster is reachable only through a Private Endpoint.

attributes.name: clustering_policy
attributes.description: Redis clustering policy. Treated as immutable here: Azure only allows it to change while the current value is `NoCluster`, so a change forces replacement rather than risking an update the API rejects. `EnterpriseCluster` is required by the RediSearch module. `NoCluster` additionally only applies to SKUs of 25 GB or less and is not supported at all by the `FlashOptimized_*` family; the API rejects both cases.

attributes.name: eviction_policy
attributes.description: Key eviction policy applied when the cache is full.

attributes.name: non_tls_access_enabled
attributes.description: Also accept plaintext Redis connections alongside TLS. Defaults to TLS-only.

attributes.name: access_keys_authentication_enabled
attributes.description: Allow classic access-key authentication. Defaults to disabled, matching Azure's guidance to use Microsoft Entra ID for new caches. While disabled, the platform's access-key read and regenerate operations return an error, because Azure rejects ListKeys outright. Can be changed in place — verified live 2026-08-04. The platform's own console cannot change it: its save payload resends the current value rather than the newly selected one, so the toggle appears to revert.

attributes.name: modules
attributes.description: Redis modules to enable, e.g. RediSearch, RedisBloom, RedisJSON, RedisTimeSeries. Immutable after creation — Azure only accepts modules when the database is first created, so a change forces replacement. RediSearch additionally requires `clustering_policy = "EnterpriseCluster"`.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Module name, e.g. `RediSearch`, `RedisBloom`, `RedisJSON`, `RedisTimeSeries`. `RediSearch` requires `clustering_policy` = EnterpriseCluster and `eviction_policy` = NoEviction; with `geo_replication` enabled, only `RediSearch` and `RedisJSON` are accepted at all.

attributes.name: args
attributes.description: Optional module configuration string, e.g. `ERROR_RATE 0.01 INITIAL_SIZE 400`.

attributes.name: reported_modules
attributes.description: Modules as Azure reports them, mirroring `modules`.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Module name.

attributes.name: args
attributes.description: Module configuration string, empty when none.

attributes.name: persistence
attributes.description: Data persistence (backup) settings. At most one of `rdb_enabled` / `aof_enabled` may be true — Azure rejects both — and whichever is enabled requires its matching frequency. Enabling either requires `high_availability = true`, and cannot be combined with `geo_replication`. That conflict is enforced at plan time against the presence of the two blocks, which is slightly stricter than the API: it also rejects a persistence block whose flags are all `false` alongside `geo_replication`, where the API would accept it. Omit the block entirely in that case — an all-`false` persistence block does nothing.

attributes.name: rdb_enabled
attributes.description: Enable RDB snapshot persistence.

attributes.name: rdb_frequency
attributes.description: Snapshot interval. Required when `rdb_enabled` is true.

attributes.name: aof_enabled
attributes.description: Enable append-only-file persistence.

attributes.name: aof_frequency
attributes.description: Append-only-file write frequency. Required when `aof_enabled` is true.

attributes.name: geo_replication
attributes.description:
Active geo-replication group membership. Immutable: any change here REPLACES the instance. Azure only accepts geo-replication settings when the database is created, so the platform rejects an edit outright and Azure answers the underlying request with an opaque 501.

Build a group by creating both members with it already configured: give the first a `group_nickname` and an empty `linked_database_arm_ids`, then create the second with the same nickname and the first's `database_id` in its link list. Azure then links both ends itself — the first database reports the second as a member without Terraform ever sending it, so `geo_replication_linked_database_ids` on the first member will show a value its own configuration does not, and a refresh reports that as an out-of-band change. Leaving `linked_database_arm_ids` empty with no nickname creates an ordinary standalone database. Verified live 2026-08-04.

Setting either field here counts as enabling geo-replication, which brings four constraints: it requires `high_availability = true`; it is rejected on the `Balanced_B0`, `Balanced_B1` and every `FlashOptimized_*` SKU; it cannot be combined with `persistence`; and the only modules it tolerates are `RediSearch` and `RedisJSON`.

WARNING: while geo-replication is enabled the instance cannot be UPDATED AT ALL — not even its tags. The platform validates geo-replication immutability by comparing the requested `linked_database_arm_ids` against Azure's reported member list within the same request body, and those two can never match: the configured list holds the peers, while Azure's holds every member including the database itself. Every update is therefore rejected with "Cannot change spec.geoReplication after creation", whatever it actually changed. This affects the platform's own console equally. Treat a geo-replicated instance as immutable and replace it to change anything. Verified live 2026-08-04.

attributes.name: group_nickname
attributes.description: Shared name identifying the geo-replication group. Required when `linked_database_arm_ids` is non-empty.

attributes.name: linked_database_arm_ids
attributes.description: Full ARM resource IDs of the other databases already in the group.

attributes.name: tags
attributes.description: Tags applied to the Redis instance. The platform adds its own managed `duplocloud-ai-*` tags server-side; those are filtered out of state so only your tags are managed by Terraform.

attributes.name: azure_resource_group_name
attributes.description: Azure resource group the cluster is created in, derived from the linked resource group.

attributes.name: unique_cloud_resource_id
attributes.description: Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the cluster, as the platform records it on the resource itself. `cluster_id` exposes the same ARM ID read from the live Azure result.

attributes.name: provisioner_type
attributes.description: Provisioner type. Assigned by the platform when unset — existing instances report `Cli`.

attributes.name: provisioner_version
attributes.description: Optional provisioner version. Left unset the API omits it, so this reads back empty rather than as an empty string.

attributes.name: status
attributes.description: Current provisioning status of the Redis instance.

attributes.name: redis_id
attributes.description: ID of this Redis instance, for reference by dependent resources.

attributes.name: cluster_id
attributes.description: Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the Redis Enterprise cluster.

attributes.name: database_id
attributes.description: Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the `default` database. Empty until the database child finishes provisioning, which happens after the cluster — set `wait_for_database` to block until it is populated.

attributes.name: provisioning_state
attributes.description: Azure provisioning state of the cluster, e.g. Succeeded or Creating.

attributes.name: host_name
attributes.description: Redis endpoint hostname, e.g. myredis.eastus.redisenterprise.cache.azure.net.

attributes.name: port
attributes.description: TCP port of the database endpoint.

attributes.name: geo_replication_group_nickname
attributes.description: Geo-replication group nickname reported by Azure, if the database belongs to a group.

attributes.name: geo_replication_linked_database_ids
attributes.description: ARM resource IDs of the other databases linked in the same geo-replication group, as reported by Azure.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the Redis instance was created (RFC 3339).

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Timestamp when the Redis instance was last updated (RFC 3339).

attributes.name: version
attributes.description: Version counter, incremented on each update.
